title: fix(models): keep large fleets responsive during model preparation
body:
Related: #149538, #148529

Thanks to @609NFT for the 632-agent reports and detailed profiles in #149538 and #148529.

## What Problem This Solves

Large fleets keep the Gateway's main thread inside `buildSnapshotBatch` on the microtask queue during model preparation and post-ready rebuilds, delaying health and status requests. The [lead's separate 632-agent × 54-model reproduction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/149538#issuecomment-5701606329) recorded a 730-second gap around bind/model preparation, a 23.4-second post-ready gap, and 22 timed-out health probes out of 300 after readiness. This PR isolates and measures the batch owner with a 200-agent reproduction.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reported profiles put 71–96% under `buildSnapshotBatch`: repeated activation/config serialization and fleet roster walks, followed by 49.5 seconds in recursive plugin argument restoration. Already-resolved promises kept that work on the microtask queue.

Preparation now captures one immutable runtime/authored config pair per fleet generation and carries its provenance forward. Activation fingerprints, roster indexes, and argument-graph analysis reuse those prepared facts. Unchanged plugin selections preserve capture identity. Nine real event-loop yields separate bounded workspace/agent/source/registry/snapshot work, with current-owner checks after yielding and auth replay tied to the credential-capture boundary.

Valid config hashing retains the lazy memo keyed by the actual deeply frozen object. Invalid diagnostic snapshots short-circuit in the reset/bootstrap comparison and `config.get` before hashing; reset still compares selected target, existence, validity, and raw revision. Valid fresh-install defaults retain their resolved revision even when the physical config file is absent. Capture records carry source/origin provenance, without eager fingerprints.

Catalog finalization now prepares the shared `{agents, plugins}` fingerprint in the existing build-local config map. Per-agent native source fingerprints combine it with that agent's selections and configured refs. Worker-generation code separately memoizes runtime/source config digests by immutable object identity, using its existing SHA-256/stable-stringify encoding; mutable worker reconstructions rehash. That separate encoding preserves distinctions such as undefined versus null. Full worker payloads, credential data, serialized SecretRef provenance, and generation checks remain intact.

Merged #149314 is already in the benchmark baseline. It covers immutable **metadata-inventory fingerprint caching** and other startup work; it does not change activation result/config hashing or plugin argument restoration. This PR complements PR A #149600 (cron skill-review reconciliation), PR B #149716 (chat metadata), and PR C #150004 (eager Codex catalog-home roster construction). PR C merged after the measured baseline; these measured revisions do not include it.

## User Impact

The pre-rebase 200-agent measurement restored model preparation near the prior fast candidate: **22.499 s** finally, versus **23.331 s** in V2, **46.531 s** in the record-based sample, and **68.872 s** before this PR. The Gateway answers health during preparation (8/23 within the phase), with phase RSS reduced to **943.9 MiB**. The final 11.950-second blocked overlap and phase-health result remain worse than the best V2 sample; this PR does not claim all startup stalls are resolved.

Explicit dev reset recovers invalid config without a WeakMap exception. No new operator setting, CLI option, dependency, schema migration, or action is required. Normal update/recovery ownership is preserved; no published-driver × candidate upgrade result is claimed.

**The 30-second full `openclaw status --json` gate is NOT fully met: 1/3 final attempts succeeded.** The separate online CLI status follow-up landed in #150269; these historical measurements do not include that change. Direct Gateway status succeeds independently; it is not a substitute for full CLI completion.

## Evidence

### Attribution of the slower sample

The 46.531-second clean sample on `01d7c3` did not reproduce during attribution: the same production code measured 21.621 seconds, while prior production measured 18.548 seconds. Counts rule out the proposed 200-capture amplification in this fixture. Both versions create one runtime/source pair during model preparation and reuse it 400 times. The record-based change adds one authored-source hash, about 5 ms, rather than 200 hashes of separate captures. The 1,600 computations on 801 other config/environment inputs are unchanged across the counter runs; the shared runtime capture itself is hashed once in every variant. The historical wall-time difference remains unattributed; single runs do not control host activity, filesystem caches, or unrelated background work.

| Through model-runtime completion | Prior production (4687) | Record-based (01d7) | Final |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Public hash calls / computations | 2,200 / 1,601 | 2,202 / 1,602 | 2,200 / 1,601 |
| Public hash computation time | 110.644 ms | 113.223 ms | 108.594 ms |
| Capture creates / reuses | 1 / 400 | 1 / 400 | 1 / 400 |
| Distinct original / authored source objects | 1 / 1 | 1 / 1 | 1 / 1 |
| Native-source full-fleet serializations | 200 | 200 | 1 shared preparation + 200 small combinations |
| Worker-generation full-fleet serializations | 200 composites containing both config graphs | 200 composites containing both config graphs | 2 shared config/source digests + 200 small combinations |
| Native-source fingerprint time | 1,213.987 ms | 1,263.658 ms | 13.211 ms (5.741 shared + 7.470 combinations) |
| Worker-generation fingerprint time | 2,623.680 ms | 2,820.393 ms | 18.241 ms (13.236 config/source + 5.005 combinations) |

Whole-boot counts through the same model-complete checkpoint were 2,230 calls / 1,631 computations for prior production, and 2,235 / 1,635 for record-based production. Both had three captures overall, three original objects, and two authored-source objects. Final whole-checkpoint public hashing is 2,230 calls / 1,631 computations (293.391 ms), with the same three capture creates and 400 reuses. Worker-config hashing makes 400 calls over two immutable objects: two computations and 398 hits. The final instrumented model phase is 14.156 seconds; its batch takes 7.933 seconds, followed by a 6.088-second synchronous committed-catalog refresh tail. That remaining scheduling work is a follow-up at `refreshCommittedProviderCatalogs` in `src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.refresh-scope.ts`; the full-roster hashing identified in catalog finalization is fixed here.

The prior production tree was materialized as a four-file overlay in the assigned worktree and verified byte-for-byte against `4687f3106744463b51f5072f8493b1dd5fdc09ad`; the Git branch/HEAD was not switched. Both initial counter windows end at model-runtime completion, before readiness. One failed probe attempt and an early-bootstrap probe-preflight overlap were retained as tooling limitations, not product failures. Counters record numeric object identities and timing only; final performance claims below use a separate uninstrumented run.

### Uninstrumented 200-agent comparison

The fixture uses 200 distinct workspaces/agent databases, 54 model refs each (10,800 total), 53 inline models and one unresolved ref, the same 12 bundled plugins, and no model turns or channel traffic. Each run uses Node 26.8.2, the same source-performance profile, isolated HOME/state, a free loopback port, an independent 10 ms timer, one health probe per second with a 5-second deadline, and three full CLI status probes with 30-second deadlines. Diagnostic-tail work is excluded from the primary post-ready window. A full gap crossing a phase boundary is reported separately from its overlap inside the phase.

The clean run had no fingerprint preload (`measurement.instrumentation` is null). The fixture manifest is identical across runs, while absolute paths differ because each run uses fresh isolated state. The final 13.843-second full gap crosses post-bind plugin loading; maximum overlap inside the phase is 11.950 seconds. A 30.286-second pre-ready gap and 6.936-second post-ready gap remain. Post-ready health completed 98/101 requests within its 100.683-second window. Final phase health and blocked overlap are not back to V2's 14/24 and 8.704 seconds. These are individual synthetic runs with host load and filesystem caches uncontrolled.

Full CLI outcomes were timeout at 30.015 s, valid JSON/exit zero at 27.112 s, and timeout at 30.017 s. A separate diagnostic attempt spent **19.938 s** in `status.config`, including **200 metadata scans totaling 18.620 s** and 200 freezes totaling 0.627 s; `status.local-agents` and `status.agent-admission` remained pending at its 30.020-second deadline. Those scan timings are nested inside config time. Separately, direct Gateway status returned independently parsed valid JSON in **2.099 s**, with a **367 ms** handler.

The follow-up entry point is `src/commands/status.scan-overview.ts:168`; its full metadata reader reaches the per-workspace loop in `src/config/io.plugin-metadata.ts:218`, followed by local admission in `src/commands/status.agent-local.ts:42`. Online status should consume the authorized Gateway's prepared status projection—admission state, session counts, heartbeat/tasks, and runtime vitals—while preserving explicit offline/local diagnostics and response scopes. This PR does not change that CLI path.

All owned Gateways and diagnostic processes exited, with the isolated ports verified closed. Final local evidence is retained under `.local/fleet-serve/l470-after-200-final9a4/`; the separate counter report is under `.local/fleet-serve/l470-fingerprint-final9a4-200/`. No remote-catalog timeout occurred in the final clean run; the synthetic missing-System-Agent memory warning remained.

### Rebase onto current main

The latest rebase moves this series onto `90b421ae252ceaea5bf5a9f106eab51bf384431b`, which includes the Control UI budget and worktree-fixture fixes from #150491 and the wrapper-inventory fix from #150453. All ten commits are patch-identical in `git range-diff`, including the inventory additions; there were no conflicts, and `git diff --check` passed. The following paragraph records the earlier mechanical rebase.

Rebased the published series from `1fdce1a4aa636b400179a0e43933d7fe52d45ddd` onto main `c32a31812663e577467453df24844aa82fb36d27`. The only conflict was `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt`: all **1,122** main entries were retained and the same two PR modules were inserted in sorted order, producing **1,124** unique entries with no deletions.

The resolution is mechanical. The first nine commits are patch-identical in `git range-diff`; the default matcher shows the tenth inventory commit as removed/re-added because its two additions now sit within main's expanded inventory. Its added paths are byte-identical to the original patch. Independent comparison also confirms unchanged added/deleted line bytes across all 51 PR files. No production hunk, fixture behavior, or main-side landing was dropped or altered by conflict resolution. Per the lead's explicit mechanical-rebase rule, no fresh autoreview was run.

All 28 requested focused files were exercised. **382 runtime/Gateway tests have passing results**, covering catalog selection, all 20 chat-metadata lifecycle cases, invalid-config recovery, config/activation/argument sharing, lifecycle transitions, and worker metadata/credential reconstruction. The initial direct catalog-integration run hit its unchanged 120-second case timeout; that result is retained. A separate run through the retained CI-native group passed and exited normally in 103.959 seconds, with no watchdog or retry; no assertion or timeout was changed.

The two tooling suites reported **133 passed, 24 failed, 2 skipped**. Fresh-main and provisioning failures include the known main-side omission of `src/plugins/discovery-availability.js`, plus observed fixture command timing/termination failures (a 30-second case timeout, Git `spawnSync ETIMEDOUT`, and two null process-status results). The known inventory owner remains with its separate lane; these results are not presented as green tooling proof.

Full `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed, including core/test typechecks, core/script lint, zero dead exports, and zero runtime import cycles. No extension-lint host substitute was needed. The resolution changes **0 production lines and 0 test lines** relative to the previously reviewed patch; it only relocates the same two tooling inventory additions within main's list.

The new source base uses its frozen lockfile. The focused runner rebuilt runtime artifacts for the rebased head; no separate full build or 200-agent benchmark is claimed for this mechanical resolution. Prior benchmark tables remain historical evidence on their recorded revisions.

### Wrapper inventory correction

The inventory follow-up `1fdce1a4aa636b400179a0e43933d7fe52d45ddd` was published first under the lead ruling. It then conflicted with newer main and could not receive a pull-request CI run; the author-owned rebase described above resolves that conflict.

The canonical source inventory in `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt` omitted two modules introduced by this PR. Main's newer provisioning wrapper reaches `src/config/runtime-snapshot.ts` and `src/config/runtime-source-projection.ts`; their runtime imports require `src/shared/immutable-data.ts` and `src/config/runtime-config-capture-state.ts`. Fresh materialized wrapper trees therefore failed with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` before the fresh-main/provisioning assertions. Both files are now included in the existing inventory. **Tooling +2/−0; production 0; tests 0.**

`src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.oauth-providers.ts` is intentionally excluded: its sole runtime importer is `src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.facts.ts`, outside the wrapper's materialized import closure. The comparator's AuthStorage import is type-only. The two added inventory files introduce no further runtime module dependencies beyond Node built-ins.

Scoped `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt` passed, including the tooling guards and script lint. Local Codex P1 review is scoped-clean. The operation-lock suite reported **139 passed, 1 failed, 1 skipped** in **219.09 seconds**. The lead accepted this proof for the inventory-only correction and classified the remaining failure as an observed host-load timeout on the shared worker host:

- Case: `scripts/pr per-PR operation lock > finishes native cleanup with linked wrapper (merge-run, failure=none)`.
- Observed case duration: **17,669 ms**. Its unchanged `spawnSync` limit is **15,000 ms**.
- Exact assertion: `expect(result.error, output).toBeUndefined()` at `test/scripts/pr-operation-lock.test.ts:1966`.
- Received: `Error { code: "ETIMEDOUT", syscall: "spawnSync .../.worktrees/pr-42/scripts/pr" }`, after the fixture printed its synthetic `MERGED` receipt.

No timeout or assertion was changed. `test/scripts/pr-worktree-provision.test.ts` is absent from this branch's base and was not run locally. It exists on newer main and runs in CI with that main-side wrapper; the lander will rebase once main is green, including the separate sibling `discovery-availability.ts` inventory correction. This follow-up does not rebase or change that sibling owner.

### Chat metadata lifecycle fixture correction

`checks-node-compact-small-19` on `b16332e9111244d9782bfce2e60b906230f2bb97` failed seven cases in `server-chat-metadata-lifecycle.integration.test.ts`. The three-argument response contract was intact: `models.list` still called `respond(true, result, undefined)`, and the third argument is the optional RPC error. The mismatch was the second argument's `available: false` after the fixture marked native discovery ready.

The seven-case synthetic readiness callback required exact identity with the authored `nativeConfig`. This PR intentionally separates the public config stamp from the captured native observation config; the previous real Gateway catalog regression established that selection must use the discovery capture. The fixture now consumes the published owner's recorded `observationConfig` and retains its strict identity guard, structural config assertion, and every response, metadata, pin-authority, generation, stamp, registry, disposal, revision, and discovery-count assertion. A local owner reader consolidates three repeated lookups and shrinks the over-cap test file by seven lines. Production is unchanged; restoring the authored identity in production would reintroduce the independently proven native selection defect.

| Attribution | File runs passed | Tests in each run |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| PR head `b16332e9111244d9782bfce2e60b906230f2bb97` | 0/3 | 13 passed, 7 failed |
| Pinned main `387f69830a81968ed2d4ef830d67456167bc7f43` | 3/3 | 20 passed, 0 failed |
| Corrected fixture | 3/3 | 20 passed, 0 failed |

Both revisions used the same assigned worktree, Node 24.21.0, two workers, and unchanged test/dependency manifests. All seven original failures were payload-availability mismatches at the same registered-handler assertion. No sleeps, retries, changed deadlines, weakened expectations, or new production seams were added. The fixture-only local P1 review is scoped-clean, and the lead accepted publication of this correction before further hang attribution. The grouped native catalog integration subsequently hit its 120-second test timeout; an explicit-project probe then hit the 120-second local no-output watchdog without a result. These failures remain recorded. The remaining focused projects, changed-file gate, and fresh committed branch review have not been completed for this correction; the CI-group attribution is recorded below. No broader validation success is claimed.

No production boundary, capture, hash, or sharing logic changed. The successful full build from the preceding correction (8m 0.6s) remains applicable; neither it nor the historical 200-agent benchmark was repeated for this test-only change.

### Native catalog hang attribution after publishing the fixture correction

The retained CI job runs `agentic-gateway-methods-hosted-1` with `gateway-methods` and `gateway-methods-isolated` configs and exactly one included file: `test/plugins/codex-model-catalog.gateway.test.ts`. The reproduction used `node --import tsx scripts/ci-run-node-test-shard.mts` with that extracted group, two workers, the CI 300-second no-output watchdog and retry setting, and the unchanged 120-second test timeout. The isolated companion config has no matching test; it exits normally as in CI.

| Revision | Passed / runs | Test timeouts | Watchdogs / retries | Test-body seconds by run |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| PR `445216f33ea26f87a72446e2eb47dd01d60e6073` | 3/3 | 0 | 0/0 | 94.700, 31.853, 29.047 |
| Pinned main `79121743a16969fd86dfd88fcd5422dacea88ac3` | 3/3 | 0 | 0/0 | 62.887, 12.673, 17.728 |

All six invocations exited normally after the passing case. Whole-command times were 325.320/95.280/133.261 seconds on the branch and 243.804/40.094/46.671 seconds on main; first invocations include runtime rebuilds. Both used local Node 24.21.0 and task-owned caches without CI's restored cache seed; each revision used its own frozen lockfile. Main's newer fs-safe dependency and peer-lock entries are a comparison difference. This is a scoped reproduction, not a fleet performance comparison or a rerun of unrelated groups packed into that CI job.

The hang did not reproduce in this CI group, so no pending owner is attributed and the head-only condition for scratch instrumentation was not met. The earlier local grouped run timed out during its only case; it did not print a passing case followed by a teardown stall. Its cause remains unproven. Read-only comparison with #150354 confirms overlapping catalog-worker, publication-join and pool-close owners, but that is not evidence that one caused these timeouts. No shared-owner production fix was made, and the unused scratch diagnostic template was not committed.

The assigned branch and its locked dependencies were restored after the comparison. CI [35167882651](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35167882651) is attached to the published fixture-correction head. The earlier incomplete broader validation is not recast as a full-suite pass.

### Rebased catalog-selection correction

The unchanged registered Gateway test in `test/plugins/codex-model-catalog.gateway.test.ts` exposed a publication defect after the rebase: native discovery recorded account/model readiness against the captured config, but `createPreparedModelRuntimeSnapshot` published the original config stamp as `observationConfig`. The native harness correctly requires the exact discovery config and plugin-config identity, so selection returned unavailable despite successful discovery. The owner now publishes `agentFacts.input.config` for observations while retaining `publishedConfig` for the public config stamp. No discovery retry, broader cache key, or auth/home-scope relaxation was added.

| Attribution, unchanged test and deadlines | Passed | Failed |

| PR head `e4035d9401faa02542d426fcff7d0fb3d49d3f22` | 0 | 10 |
| Pinned main `f542d35411621a9f2b17fa0186cb14880b83c976` | 10 | 0 |
| Repaired source, original Gateway test | 1 | 0 |

Both comparisons ran in the assigned worktree with Node 24.21.0, the `gateway-methods` project, two workers, and identical test/manifest/lock/project configuration. Every branch failure was the original line-191 availability assertion. One additional main invocation produced no test result: the existing 120-second no-output watchdog terminated it after worker preparation took 79 seconds. Its exit-143 log is retained separately; the watchdog and assertions were unchanged. CI uses Linux Node 24.19.0, so local comparison does not replace CI.

The new colocated regression awaits completed catalog loading and then evaluates the recorded readiness facts without polling. It failed pre-fix with `availability: false` instead of `true`, and passes after the owner repair. It also verifies the public stamp, model-neutral stamp advancement, cloned-config and agent-directory isolation, and revocation. **361 focused tests across 24 files pass**, including previous lifecycle, invalid-config recovery, worker reconstruction, and chat-metadata regressions. The original Gateway integration passes through its later refresh/account-change/revocation assertions. `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed completely, with core/test typechecks, lint, zero dead exports and zero runtime import cycles; no extension-lint host substitute was needed. Full `pnpm build` passed in **8m 0.6s**. Fresh Codex autoreview `--mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P1` is **scoped-clean** on `b16332e9111244d9782bfce2e60b906230f2bb97`.

This correction changes no capture shape, hashing, sharing key, or scheduling logic. The 200-agent table above is retained evidence from pre-rebase `9a4f5e11cf50a74cca1dcfe6bd9da52295385b4b`; it was not remeasured on this rebased correction. It is not a new performance or CLI-responsiveness claim.

### Earlier regression and validation (before rebase)

The retained pre-fix invalid-reset result is:

```text
TypeError: Invalid value used as weak map key
  hashRuntimeConfigValue src/config/runtime-snapshot.ts:191
  recheckGatewayRunReset src/cli/gateway-cli/pre-bootstrap.ts:444
```

Restoring the prior memo before applying diagnostic guards reproduces four failures: the original CLI case plus absent/null/string source cases. Raw-content and file-target drift refusals pass. After the owner fix, all six cases pass **10/10 each (60/60)**. Additional config-response coverage verifies invalid diagnostics avoid hashing and valid fresh-install defaults retain applied revision equality.

Boundary negatives also reproduce 201 full-config hashes instead of one for an uncaptured immutable config, 400 roster projections instead of two, 9→17 whole-roster digests as the fixture grows from 8→16 agents, and 33 worker config digests instead of one. The corrected code passes those bounds, keeps roster/plugin mutation and per-agent selection/ref invalidation, and preserves independently reconstructed worker fingerprints, including undefined/null and authored SecretRef distinctions. Catalog mutation tests request real catalog refresh before reading completed-discovery facts.

**360 focused tests across 24 files pass**, including the prior lifecycle and chat-metadata CI regressions. The three catalog-sharing cases passed again after an import-only cleanup. `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed completely, including typechecks, lint, dead exports, and zero runtime import cycles; no extension-lint host substitute was needed. `pnpm build` passed (10m 15.8s), the matching `sourcePerformance` build passed (57.4s), and fresh Codex autoreview `--mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P1` is scoped-clean on the committed head.

### Hash entry-point audit

| Entry point | Value type / admission boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Runtime snapshot publication, source capture, cache key and write notifications | Config/source records supplied by their owners; deeply frozen objects share lazy hashes, mutable objects rehash. Capture accepts config objects and carries source/origin provenance. |
| Gateway CLI `pre-bootstrap.ts` comparison | Invalid diagnostic source can be absent/null/non-object. These snapshots compare target/existence/validity/raw revision and short-circuit before hashing. Valid normalized source objects retain hash comparison. |
| `gateway/config-get-response.ts` | Invalid snapshots return no resolved revision and never enter hashing; raw revision, issues and current applied revision remain available. Valid defaults, including a missing physical file, still hash their normalized source object. |
| Config reload, Doctor preflight checkpoint, system-agent execution | Existing validity/admission checks precede hashing of config/source records. |
| Prepared-runtime owner, inbound registry and facts | Config/environment records; prepared config objects are immutable captures. Optional environment inputs are guarded/defaulted. |
| Models config, provider-auth and auth-provider config | Discovery/environment records, `ModelAuthAvailabilityRef` objects via the existing cast, and explicitly constructed provider wrappers. |
| Transcript reload | Explicit config wrapper object. |
| Activation reuse | Mixed components; existing object narrowing precedes its memo, primitives follow its pure hash path. |
| Plugin argument restoration | Graph traversal returns for primitives before weak access. |
| Runtime reader and roster facts | Reader only looks up capture provenance. Roster memo keys immutable config objects, checks external legacy-owner metadata, and retains callback-local batching for mutable configs. |
| Worker generation | Config/source object leaves use the existing stable-facts encoding and an immutable-identity memo. Mutable reconstructed worker objects are independently hashed; no diagnostic inputs enter this owner. |
